prompts.prompt: Name a determinant of price elasticity of demand

answers.why: More close substitutes means buyers switch easily, so demand is more elastic.
Necessities have inelastic demand; people buy them whatever the price.
The bigger the share of income a good takes, the more elastic its demand.
Demand gets more elastic over time as buyers find alternatives.
Narrowly defined goods (one brand) are more elastic than broad ones (all food).
Purchases of durables can be postponed, so demand is more price elastic.
S in STORES: a subsidy lowers costs, supply shifts right.
S in STORES: an indirect tax raises costs, supply shifts left.
T in STORES: better technology lowers costs.
O in STORES: joint supply (beef/leather) or competitive supply.
R in STORES: dearer inputs shift supply left.
E in STORES: expected price rises can cut supply now.
S in STORES: more firms, more supply.

cards.back: As price rises, quantity supplied rises, ceteris paribus.

quiz.explain: |PED| < 1, so quantity changes proportionally less than price.
